The **String** standard library slices and searches text. On the bundled log
`sample_data/app.log`, you can filter lines and count them — a common
verification when checking logs for errors. `Get Lines Containing String` keeps
only the matching lines; `Get Line Count` counts them.

## Task 1 — Count the error lines in the log

**Goal:** create `checks/string.robot` that reads the log, filters it to the
`ERROR` lines, and asserts how many there are.

Here is the same filter-and-count over a small built-up string (no file needed).
Adapt it to read the log instead.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    String

*** Test Cases ***
Count Matching Lines
    ${text}=    Catenate    SEPARATOR=\n    apple    error    banana    error
    ${matches}=    Get Lines Containing String    ${text}    error
    ${count}=    Get Line Count    ${matches}
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${count}    2
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite imports `String` and defines `Count Error Lines In The Log`.

<!-- hint -->
Read the log first — you'll need `OperatingSystem` too:
`${log}=    Get File    sample_data/app.log`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Filter to the error lines with `Get Lines Containing String    ${log}    ERROR`,
count with `Get Line Count`, and assert the count is `3`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    String
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Count Error Lines In The Log
    ${log}=    Get File    sample_data/app.log
    ${errors}=    Get Lines Containing String    ${log}    ERROR
    ${count}=    Get Line Count    ${errors}
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${count}    3
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the log has exactly three error lines.
